In comparison to even the most sophisticated industrial robots, creating a successful humanoid requires solving tremendous engineering challenges, as dozens of motion axes must work dynamically together with minimal power consumption, at optimal torque, in perfect harmony. Better Humanoid Motion, From Design to Delivery Humanoid robots must navigate unpredictable terrain, carrying their own power source and the combined weight of their actuators and other components — while manipulating objects ranging from lightweight, precision tools to large, heavy packages. Performing tasks with human-like dexterity requires precise motion of interdependent robotic joints coordinated across a robust skeletal structure. Frameless motors designed specifically for the torque, acceleration, size and weight requirements of robotic joints are key to achieving the necessary kinematic performance and energy efficiency. Learn how to specify these motors using a system-level strategy while ensuring the manufacturability you need to progress smoothly from prototype to full production. Read the White Paper Lightweight, Torque-Dense, Robot-Ready Motion To design battery-operated humanoids that reliably carry their own weight while performing heavy work for extended periods of time, you need highly responsive and precise frameless servo motors that deliver all the required torque across a wide speed range. But that’s not all. To enable robotic joints that operate at a human scale, in the real world, servo motors must deliver exceptional performance in a package that minimizes size and weight, while maximizing power at an affordable cost. Learn how to identify the unique challenges of humanoid motion and how to solve them with motors designed to be robot ready. Read the Blog Motion Control Fundamentals for Humanoids & Exoskeletons As humanoid technology matures, established robotics companies and startups see endless opportunities for replicating and improving upon human capabilities in warehouse logistics, healthcare, manufacturing, construction, service industries and more. To win in these emerging humanoid markets, robot engineers need to address issues of performance, cost and scalability simultaneously. Learn how to design motion for humanoids that perform optimally not only in prototype but also in the commercial arena.
